prerequisites: Fundamentals of electrical and mechanical vibrations

learning_outcomes.text: Apply knowledge of vibrations from Technical Mechanics and the "Electrical Engineering and Measurement Technology" module to vibration measurement in machines and systems. Understand the mode of action and interaction of mechatronic components (mechanical, electronic, and programmed components).

Use the results of vibration measurements to make statements about the condition of machines and systems. This applies to safety-oriented monitoring (with the goal of shutdown) as well as preventive measurements (with the goal of optimizing maintenance cycles). Apply knowledge to increase efficiency and conserve resources.

syllabus_topics: Introduction: Basic concepts and origin of vibrations, including repetition of forced vibrations, modes, etc.

Motivation: Vibration measurement as part of preventive and safety-oriented monitoring of machines and systems. Comparison of measurements with acceleration sensors and microphones (acceleration vs. sound).
Measurement of vibrations with accelerometers and microphones (reaction-free, frequency range, amplitude range, directional microphones, sound power level of machines)

Evaluation of vibration data (characteristic values, trends, FFT) for preventive and safety-oriented monitoring (condition monitoring and safety monitoring). Damage frequencies of rolling bearings, gears, or fans are considered, especially with regard to preventive maintenance. Integration of measurements into plant operation.
Modeling and metrological characterization using the example of a loudspeaker:
Modeling of chassis, housing, and crossover with concentrated components
Coupling between mechanical and acoustic system
Measures for active and passive vibration and noise reduction
assessment_rules: The graded assessment is an oral examination. The duration of the oral examination is subject to the currently valid General Part of the Examination Regulations (ATPO). The ungraded assessment is an experimental work, which includes 2-4 experiments.
